# WO-505: CLI JSON: a PII-free "bundle check" document

Vendor: grok
Agent: backend-core (Derek Olsen)
Owner contact: Morgan Reyes (check-ins via GROK_TO_CLAUDE.md)
Kind: engine
Epic: E1 (docs/vendor/EPICS.md)
Target release: 0.4
Source: in-house 0.4 epic batch 2026-11-09 (in-house offline until about Nov 14; vendors keep working the queue in epic order)
Worktree: none until unblocked (then `.vendor-wt/wo-505` on `vendor/wo-505` from main)
Tracker: issue pending (in-house syncs freemyid-pm)
Order: start only after WO-340, WO-357, WO-502 are merged (they share a file or a behaviour this builds on); rebase on main first.

## Goal
Give scripts and the helper's tools a stable, PII-free JSON report for a bundle file, built from the WO-501 and WO-502 helpers, following the existing document builders (`failure_doc`, `cli_json.py:197-200`, and `registry_doc`, `cli_json.py:120-139`). Starts only after the contract exists.

## Blocked: what in-house must provide first
In-house must (1) add the `bundle_check/1` JSON schema under `schema/` and register it in the `--json` contract, (2) add the `freemyid bundle check FILE [--json]` command in `cli.py` that calls the WO-501/502 helpers and `cli_json.emit`, and (3) add the `docs/CLI.md` section so Grok can write `bundle_check_doc(header, doc_check, plan_lines) -> dict` in `cli_json.py` against a fixed shape. Suggested shape: `{"schema": "bundle_check/1", "ok": bool, "header": code, "problems": [str], "counts": {"addresses": n, "phones": n, "emails": n, "relatives": n}, "has_birth_year": bool, "scope": "all|phone|email"}`. No names or values ever appear in it. Exit codes use `EXIT_OK`/`EXIT_USAGE` (`cli_json.py:25-29`).

Not startable by a vendor. In-house unblocks it by changing the status line and posting a GO.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)
1. `bundle_check_doc` returns exactly the agreed keys for ok, header-failed and document-failed inputs (golden dict per case).
2. A guard test walks every string in the document for sentinel values from a fake profile; none may appear.
3. The key order and types match the schema file (test loads `schema/bundle_check.schema.json` once in-house adds it).
4. Existing `cli_json` tests and WO-340 guard pass unchanged.

**Limits (every Grok WO, CLAUDE-G-004):** offline only. No network, credentials, git or gh, installs, or running the real app against real sites or a real mailbox; never read anything outside the repo. Fake people only (Jane Q Testperson, Springfield IL). Tests pass on Windows too (`tmp_path`, `pathlib`). Check `tests/copilot/`, `tests/codex/`, `tests/grok/` and the in-house `tests/test_*.py` first; don't duplicate a guard.

Code rules (backend WOs; owner lane change 2026-11-09):
- Change only the listed `src/` files and the new test file. No contract changes: `models.py`, `interfaces.py`, `state.py`, `registry.py`, `storage/`, `schema/`, `cli.py`, `config.py`, `paths.py`, `netpolicy.py`, `consent.py`, `crypto.py`, `secrets.py`, `secret_backends.py`, `logging_setup.py`, `engine/browser.py`. If the work needs one of them, stop and write "needs in-house contract change first" in VENDOR_STATUS.md and your GROK-NNN.
- Front end and design stay in-house: never `src/freemyid/wizard/`, `src/freemyid/templates/`, `web/`, `brand/`.
- Offline: tests use fakes and `monkeypatch`. An autouse fixture in your test file makes `socket.socket.connect` and `socket.create_connection` raise. No subprocess, no real scheduler, browser or mailbox. Never run `freemyid run`, `send` or `schedule install`.
- Every existing test keeps passing unchanged. If your change correctly breaks an in-house or Codex test, stop and report it with file:line; never edit a test outside your allowed paths.
- Typed Python 3.11+, ruff-clean, small focused diff. Logs and events stay PII-free (counts and codes only). Fake people only. Line numbers are from main at the time of writing (2026-11-09); re-check them.
